content: Dimethylaminoethanol (DMAE), also referred to as dimethylethanolamine (DMEA), is a primary alcohol. It is also known by other chemical names, including N,N-dimethyl-2-aminoethanol, beta-dimethylaminoethyl alcohol, beta-hydroxyethyldimethylamine, and Deanol. This compound appears as a transparent, pale-yellow liquid. From a biochemical perspective, dimethylaminoethanol is structurally related to choline and has been proposed as a potential biochemical precursor to the neurotransmitter acetylcholine. However, this hypothesis has been contested, particularly based on findings from a 1977 rat study. While it is commonly believed that DMAE undergoes methylation in the brain to form choline, experimental evidence in rats has demonstrated that this is not the case. Instead, DMAE is metabolized in the liver to produce choline. However, the resulting choline molecule is charged and unable to cross the blood-brain barrier. Within the brain, DMAE is incorporated into phospholipids, replacing choline to form phosphatidyl-dimethylaminoethanol. This compound is subsequently integrated into nerve membranes, where it enhances membrane fluidity and permeability and exhibits antioxidant properties. Industrially, dimethylaminoethanol serves as a curing agent for polyurethanes and epoxy resins. It is also utilized in large quantities for water treatment and, to a lesser extent, in the coatings industry. Additionally, it plays a role in the synthesis of dyestuffs, textile auxiliaries, pharmaceuticals, emulsifiers, and corrosion inhibitors. DMAE is an additive in products such as paint removers, boiler water, and amino resins. It forms various salts with melting points below room temperature (ionic liquids), such as N,N-dimethylethanolammonium acetate and N,N-dimethylethanolammonium octanoate, which are used as alternatives to conventional solvents. Furthermore, 2-dimethylaminoethyl chloride hydrochloride, a derivative of DMAE, is widely employed as an intermediate in pharmaceutical manufacturing. In biomedical research, short-term studies have indicated that DMAE, when combined with vitamins and minerals, can enhance vigilance, alertness, and mood in individuals with borderline emotional disturbances. Research into its potential benefits for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) has shown promise but remains inconclusive. However, one study found that DMAE reduced the average lifespan of aged quail. A specific form of DMAE, 2-dimethylaminoethanol (+)-bitartrate, is marketed as a dietary supplement. This white powder contains 37% DMAE.
